author: Mark Atwood
text:
ESCALATING TO HUMAN — scope decision needed.

Analysis: introducing TimeZoneId(String) newtype solely on the two CalendarEventGetArgs.time_zone / CalendarEventQueryArgs.time_zone fields (the bead's literal scope) would create a *more* incoherent surface than current state. The same wire field name 'timeZone' appears as:

- Option<String> in jmap-jscalendar-types::RecurrenceRule.time_zone (RFC 8984, line 254)
- Option<String> in jmap-calendars-types::Calendar.time_zone (line 142)
- Option<String> in jmap-calendars-types::CalendarEvent.time_zone (line 278)
- Option<String> in jmap-calendars-types::CalendarEvent.recurrence_id_time_zone (line 198)
- Option<String> in jmap-calendars-server::CalendarEventGetArgs.time_zone (the bead target)
- Option<String> in jmap-calendars-server::CalendarEventQueryArgs.time_zone (the bead target)

Typing only the last two creates a half-typed surface where 'what the backend method receives as an argument' is typed but 'what the data object holds on the wire' is stringy. Future tasks-types (planned JMAP-yfpq) and any future tz-bearing extensions would compound the asymmetry.

Three coherent paths:

(a) Workspace-wide: add TimeZoneId(String) to jmap-jscalendar-types (the RFC 8984 canonical owner of the concept), propagate to all six (eventually seven, with tasks) sites. Pre-1.0 free; deferred = SemVer break per consumer.

(b) Calendars-only: add TimeZoneId to jmap-calendars-types, use in the four calendars-types fields + the two calendars-server fields. Leaves jscalendar-types RecurrenceRule.time_zone as String — accept the asymmetry as 'jscalendar owns its own grammar'.

(c) Server-only (bead literal scope): typed in the two server args, stringy everywhere else. NOT recommended — creates the half-typed surface above.

Validation question: workspace dep policy on jmap-calendars-server is 'jmap-types, jmap-calendars-types, jmap-server, serde_json, thiserror'. Adding chrono-tz for IANA-name membership validation is OUT of policy. A TimeZoneId(String) with only structural validation (non-empty, plausible chars) provides type discipline without enforcement — same posture as Id and UTCDate.

Recommendation: option (a) — propagate from jmap-jscalendar-types as the canonical owner. Pre-1.0 the rename is free. Pair with a follow-up sweep bead for downstream propagation.

Note: I am NOT taking action; this is a workspace-architectural decision (which crate owns TimeZoneId?) that crosses a half-dozen public-API surfaces and requires human direction.

The TimeZoneId concept also intersects with the workspace AGENTS.md 'Externally-owned-schema classifier strings are also EXCLUDED' rule (the IANA Time Zone Database is exactly an externally-owned classifier registry). The exclusion rule is narrowly about typed-enum-with-Other(String) patterns, not about Newtype(String). But the underlying tension is the same: pretending to enforce something we cannot enforce.
